headline: Revenue growth and cost discipline swing Zillow to profit
summary_short: Zillow's revenue rose 18% y/y to $708 million and net income swung to $46 million from $8 million a year ago, as Mortgages (+56%) and Rentals (+42%) revenue growth outpaced a 3% rise in operating expenses.
summary_long: Total revenue grew 18% y/y to $708 million, led by Mortgages (+56%) on higher loan origination volume and Rentals (+42%) on rising unique visitors and revenue per visitor; Residential grew 8%. Cost of revenue rose 36% y/y, mostly higher lead-acquisition costs tied to the Redfin rentals syndication deal, pulling gross margin to 73% from 77%. Operating expenses grew just 3%, so operating income swung to $36 million from a $9 million loss and net income rose to $46 million from $8 million. Operating cash flow nearly doubled to $200 million. Cash fell to $678 million from $768 million after $626 million in share buybacks under a newly expanded $1.25 billion authorization.

drivers.explanation: Grew 18% y/y to $708M: Residential +8% on higher revenue per visit, Mortgages +56% on higher loan origination volume, Rentals +42% on rising unique visitors and revenue per visitor.
Increase tracks the revenue gain, but gross margin fell to 73% from 77% because cost of revenue grew faster than revenue.
Rose $50M (36%) y/y, primarily $38M higher lead-acquisition costs tied to the Redfin rentals syndication agreement, plus mortgage processing, ad-serving, and software costs.
Swung to $36M from a $9M loss as revenue grew 18% while total operating expenses grew just 3%.
Tracks the operating-income swing, partially offset by $6M lower other income (interest income) and $2M of income tax expense versus none a year ago.
Tracks net income growth combined with a 6.5% smaller diluted share count from ongoing buybacks.
Nearly doubled to $200M from $104M, driven by higher net income plus timing-related working-capital changes, including a $32M increase in accounts payable and $23M in accrued expenses.
Fell as $626M was spent on share buybacks and $29M on net master-repurchase-agreement repayments, partially offset by $200M of operating cash flow and $420M of net investment maturities and sales.
Declined as $633M of share repurchases outweighed $46M of net income, $95M of share-based compensation expense, and $18M of option-exercise proceeds.
Fell 6.5% y/y as buybacks (3.8M Class A plus 9.7M Class C shares repurchased this quarter) outpaced RSU vesting and option issuance.

Industry TTV grew only 2% y/y per NAR data; management said Zillow's own revenue growth exceeded industry performance, crediting continued investment across Premier Agent, Zillow Home Loans, and the multifamily rentals marketplace.
